name: scope-detector-v1
declared: 2026-10-08, before the detector was run on any case
purpose: Offline check: can publisher section headings flag cited passages whose specialised scope (reason code or named subtype) the question never established? Advisory only; it never authorises or excludes evidence.
inputs: Saved independent review bundle (development cases only). No model calls. Holdout not read.

rule.qualifier_codes: 4-digit reason codes (4xxx) in the deepest heading below chapter level that contains any such code
rule.established_if: the code appears as a whole number in the question text, or the phrase appears in the question text (case-insensitive)
rule.flagged_if: any qualifier of the cited passage is not established

applicability_rating_source: manual-review-batch-0*.json faithfulness_applicability (assisted; 0 for E13/E22/E23; 1 for E25/E29/E53; 2 for 34 cases)

thresholds.T2_control_false_flags: 0 flagged cited passages in E10, E30, E46
thresholds.T3_false_flag_rate: at most 3 of the 34 cases rated applicability 2 contain any flagged cited passage

decision_rule: Pass only if T1, T2 and T3 all hold. If any fails, record the detector as rejected for this version; revisions get a new version number and are not tuned on these results.
descriptive_only: Report flags for E23, E25, E29, E53 and the full list of flagged cases; no threshold.
limits: Assisted ratings are the reference, not independent truth
Heading qualifiers cannot confirm that a merchant is in a participating country; absence of a flag is not evidence of applicability
Visa, Adyen, PayPal and Square sources use few reason codes, so the rule mostly speaks to the Mastercard guide
